examples.en: I couldn't do my homework because of laziness.
Stop being lazy and get up quickly.

examples.ko: 아침마다 게으름이 저를 이불 속에 붙잡아요.
examples.en: Every morning laziness keeps me in my blanket.
Everyone has a bit of laziness.
I exercise every day to get out of laziness.
On weekends a little laziness is sometimes needed too.

explain: '게으름을 피우다', '게으름을 부리다'처럼 써요. 사람의 성격을 말할 때는 형용사 '게으르다'를 쓰는데, '게을러요'처럼 모양이 바뀌는 르 불규칙이에요.

phrases.example: 저는 아침에 늦게 일어나는 게으른 사람이에요.
phrases.en: I'm a lazy person who gets up late in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성격을 말할 때는 명사 '게으름' 대신 형용사 '게으르다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: To describe character, use the adjective '게으르다' instead of the noun.

phrases.en: I've been so lazy lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: '게으르다'는 르 불규칙이라 '게을러요'로 바뀌어요.
phrases.nuance_en: '게으르다' is irregular and becomes '게을러요'.

phrases.en: On weekends I laze around at home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 쉬거나 일을 미루는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes slacking off or putting things off on purpose.
phrases.en_equiv: to be lazy; to slack off

explain_en: It pairs with '게으름을 피우다' and '게으름을 부리다'. To describe a person use the adjective '게으르다', which is a 르-irregular adjective and becomes '게을러요'.

examples.ko: 겨울잠을 자는 개구리는 땅속에서 봄을 기다려요.
examples.en: Frogs that hibernate wait for spring underground.
Snakes also hibernate when winter comes.

examples.ko: 곰은 겨울잠에 들어가기 전에 많이 먹어요.
examples.en: Bears eat a lot before they go into hibernation.

examples.ko: 겨울잠 자는 동물은 어떤 게 있어요?
examples.en: What kinds of animals hibernate?

examples.ko: 겨울잠에서 깬 곰은 배가 많이 고플 거예요.
examples.en: A bear that has woken from hibernation must be very hungry.

examples.ko: 저도 겨울잠을 자고 싶을 만큼 겨울에는 졸려요.
examples.en: I get so sleepy in winter that I feel like hibernating too.

explain: '겨울잠을 자다'가 기본 표현이에요. 사람이 겨울에 너무 졸리거나 집에만 있을 때 농담으로 '겨울잠 자고 싶다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: Bears hibernate during the winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 겨울을 보내는 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic expression for animals spending the winter asleep.

phrases.en: When spring comes, frogs wake up from hibernation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겨울잠이 끝나고 일어나는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes waking up when hibernation ends.

phrases.en: It's so cold that I want to hibernate.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 추위나 졸음 때문에 농담처럼 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A joking remark people make when cold or sleepy.

explain_en: The basic expression is '겨울잠을 자다'. People also joke '겨울잠 자고 싶다' when they feel very sleepy or stay home all winter.

examples.ko: 두 나라는 긴 국경선을 맞대고 있어요.
examples.en: The two countries share a long border.
Villages near the border are quiet.

examples.ko: 국경선을 넘을 때 여권을 보여 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to show your passport when crossing the border.
On the map, the border is drawn as a dotted line.
The border runs along the river.
There is a checkpoint at the border.

explain: 그냥 '국경'이라고도 많이 말해요. '국경을 넘다'는 자주 쓰는 표현이고, 지도의 선을 말할 때 '국경선'이 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 기차를 타고 국경을 넘어 다른 나라로 갔어요.
phrases.en: I took a train across the border to another country.
phrases.nuance_ko: '국경선'보다 일상에서 더 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more often in daily life than 국경선.

phrases.example: 국경선을 따라 걸으면 작은 마을이 나와요.
phrases.en: If you walk along the border line, you reach a small village.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선의 모양을 따라 움직일 때 '따라'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses 따라 when moving along the line.

phrases.example: 이 강이 두 나라의 국경선이 돼요.
phrases.en: This river forms the border between the two countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강이나 산이 나라를 나누는 경계일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a river or mountain divides countries.

explain_en: People also often just say '국경'. '국경을 넘다' (cross the border) is a common phrase, while '국경선' fits when talking about the line on a map.

en: to be so; to be as such; to be like that

examples.en: I think so too.
It was like that in the past, too.
Everyone has times like that.
It will be the same from now on.
Because that was the situation, nobody objected.
It's always like that during exam season, isn't it?

explain: 말할 때는 '그래요', '그렇다'를 더 많이 써요. '그러하다'는 글이나 격식 있는 말에서 보여요. '그러한'과 '그러해서'는 '그런', '그래서'로 줄여 말하는 일이 많아요.

phrases.en: That's not the case for me.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그렇다'를 부정하는 활용형으로, 어떤 말이 맞지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when something is not the case.

phrases.en: I feel the same way.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그렇다'의 해요체로, 일상 대화에서 가장 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form of 그렇다, most common in daily conversation.

phrases.en: There is no such thing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '그러한'을 줄인 말로, 뒤의 명사를 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 그러한 that describes the noun after it.

explain_en: In everyday speech '그래요' and '그렇다' are more common. 그러하다 shows up in writing and formal speech. '그러한' and '그러해서' are often shortened to '그런' and '그래서' in conversation.

examples.en: I couldn't hide my surprise.
Surprise and joy mixed together at the sudden news.

examples.ko: 아이들은 놀람 반 기쁨 반으로 선물을 열었어요.
examples.en: The children opened the gift half in surprise and half in joy.

examples.ko: 놀람 때문에 한동안 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: I couldn't speak for a while because of the shock.

examples.ko: 그 소식은 우리에게 큰 놀람을 주었어요.
examples.en: That news gave us a big surprise.
A look of surprise filled his face.

explain: 말할 때는 보통 '놀랐어요'처럼 동사를 쓰고, 명사 '놀람'은 글이나 감정을 설명할 때 나와요. '놀라움'은 감탄이나 대단하다는 느낌이 있고, '놀람'은 깜짝 놀라는 느낌에 더 가까워요. '놀람을 금치 못하다'는 뉴스에서 쓰는 표현이에요.

phrases.en: I felt amazement when I saw the child's drawing.
phrases.nuance_ko: '놀람'보다 대단하다는 감탄의 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Compared with 놀람, it carries a feeling of amazement or admiration.

phrases.en: I was very surprised when the door suddenly opened.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 명사 '놀람'보다 동사 '놀라다'를 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In speech, the verb 놀라다 is used more often than the noun 놀람.

phrases.en: My friend looked at me with a surprised face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀란 표정을 설명할 때 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A natural way to describe a surprised expression.

explain_en: In speech people usually use the verb, as in '놀랐어요', and the noun '놀람' appears in writing or when describing feelings. '놀라움' carries a sense of wonder or admiration, while '놀람' is closer to being startled. '놀람을 금치 못하다' is an expression used in the news.

en: to bring onto the scene; to introduce (a character)

examples.ko: 감독은 영화 마지막에 새 인물을 등장시켰어요.
examples.en: The director brought in a new character at the end of the film.
The writer brings a cute animal into the story.

examples.ko: 무대에 가수를 등장시킬 때 조명을 어둡게 해요.
examples.en: When the singer is brought on stage, they dim the lights.
We're going to feature a famous actor in the ad.
I thought about how to introduce a new character.

examples.ko: 마술사가 상자에서 토끼를 등장시키고 박수를 받았어요.
examples.en: The magician made a rabbit appear from the box and got applause.

explain: '등장하다'는 스스로 나타나는 것이고, '등장시키다'는 사람이 어떤 인물이나 물건을 나오게 할 때 써요. 영화, 드라마, 소설, 광고 이야기에서 주로 들어요. 일상에서 사람을 데려올 때는 '데리고 오다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The director introduced the main character in the first scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 이야기에 중요한 인물을 나오게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a creator makes an important character appear in a story.
phrases.en_equiv: to bring in the main character

phrases.en: The company put a famous actor in its ad.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건을 광고에 나오게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone or something is made to appear in an ad.

phrases.example: 이 드라마는 나쁜 사람을 등장시키지 않아요.
phrases.en: This drama doesn't have any bad characters in it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 인물을 일부러 넣지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a character is deliberately left out.

explain_en: 등장하다 is when someone appears on their own, while 등장시키다 is when a person makes a character or object appear. You mostly hear it when talking about movies, dramas, novels, and ads. In daily life, for bringing a person along, use 데리고 오다.

examples.en: Oh my goodness, I left my wallet at home.
Good heavens! It's already ten o'clock.
Oh my, good heavens. What is all this?
I cried out, "Good heavens!"
I saw my test score and said, "Oh my goodness."
Oh, good heavens, we're really in trouble.

explain: '세상에', '어머'와 비슷하게 놀랐을 때 해요. 주로 곤란하거나 나쁜 일을 봤을 때 써요.

phrases.en: Oh my, is it raining this much?
phrases.nuance_ko: '맙소사'와 비슷하게 놀랐을 때 해요. 좋은 일이나 나쁜 일에 다 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '맙소사' when surprised, but works for good or bad news.

phrases.en: Oh my, is it already this late?
phrases.nuance_ko: 주로 여자들이 가볍게 놀랄 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A light expression of surprise, used more often by women.

phrases.en: Oh no, we're in trouble! I don't have the key.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤란한 일을 말할 때 '큰일 났어요'를 뒤에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '큰일 났어요' after it to say there is a serious problem.

explain_en: Like 세상에 and 어머, it is said when you are shocked. It mostly goes with troublesome or bad events.

en: to be safe; to be intact

examples.en: My whole family is safe.
There was an accident, but luckily I was unharmed.
I heard the news that the child is safe.
Seeing you safe puts my mind at ease.
I'm worried whether he is safe.
I hope the luggage arrives safely.

explain: 사고나 위험 뒤에 사람이 다치지 않고 괜찮을 때 써요. 장소나 상황이 위험하지 않다고 말할 때는 '안전하다'를 써요. '무사히 도착했어요'처럼 부사 '무사히'로도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: The plane arrived safely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무사하다'를 부사로 바꾼 말이고 도착, 귀국 같은 말과 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, often used with words like arrive or return.

phrases.en: I hope my friend who is traveling is safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 걱정되는 사람이 괜찮기를 바랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to wish that a person you worry about is safe.

phrases.en: I'm glad everyone is safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 일 뒤에 사람이 괜찮아서 안심할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express relief that people are safe after something dangerous.

explain_en: It is used for a person who came through an accident or danger without harm. To say that a place or situation is not dangerous, use 안전하다. The adverb 무사히 is also common, as in 무사히 도착했어요.

p.n: 안전하다 says the child is now in a safe state, but loses the sense of having come through the accident unharmed.

examples.en: The incident is reported in the news.
The news of the accident was reported in the morning.
What was reported turned out not to be true.
It will be reported in tomorrow's newspaper.
News about the typhoon keeps being reported.

examples.ko: 크게 보도돼서 많은 사람이 알게 됐어요.
examples.en: It was widely reported, so many people found out.

explain: 방송과 신문이 사건을 알릴 때 쓰는 말이에요. 기자나 방송사가 주인이면 '보도하다', 소식이 주인이면 '보도되다'예요. '보도 자료'는 기관이 기자들에게 주는 글이에요.

phrases.en: That story is on the news.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보도되다'를 쉬운 말로 바꾼 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier way to say 보도되다.

phrases.en: The accident was widely reported.
phrases.nuance_ko: 많은 방송과 신문이 다뤘다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means many broadcasts and papers covered it.

phrases.en: That incident hasn't been reported yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 뉴스에 나오지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Negative form meaning it hasn't appeared in the news yet.

explain_en: Used when the press announces an event. With a reporter or broadcaster as subject it is the active verb; with the news as subject it is this passive. A press release is the related noun phrase.
